prediction_scored: hit: ratio 0.904 (0.847-0.965) inside 0.70-0.95 with upper bound below 1.00 (margin 0.035). The placebo makes the causal reading doubtful (see notes).
notes: Exploratory, written after the registered result was seen (analyses/turn_restrictions/did_explore.py): a placebo installation 12 months early gives a ratio of 0.9339 (0.8607-1.0133), so treated sites were already declining relative to later-treated sites before installation. Extending that pre-installation trend gives a trend-adjusted ratio of 1.0425 (0.8692-1.2504). The likely cause is the comparison group: DOT chooses sites after crash clusters, so treated sites are past their peak while later-treated sites in the same calendar months are still approaching theirs. The registered ratio therefore mixes any treatment effect with regression to the mean in opposite directions in the two groups. Checks fixed in did.py: 30 m radius 0.8953; cohorts avoiding March-June 2020 0.9 (0.8213-0.9863). Treated sites: 3,242 left-turn crashes before, 2,683 after. 'Making Left Turn' records halve citywide from 2019 to 2020 (24,582 to 12,636 vehicles); calendar-matched controls absorb this.

graph_effect.label: No graph evaluation of turn calming or turn bans. settle: A design that separates the treatment from regression to the mean: empirical Bayes before-after with a safety performance function, or a comparison group of untreated signalized intersections matched on the crash history DOT used for selection, registered before the data are read. DOT's site-selection lists (which crash years it used) would let the selection window be excluded.
